question: The strong, gusty, hot, dry winds blowing during the day over the north and northwestern India in summer are known as ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Loo**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Loo** refers to the strong, gusty, hot, dry winds that blow during the day over the north and northwestern parts of India during the summer season.
 
• These winds are extremely hot and can cause severe heat waves, leading to heatstroke and other health issues.
 
• They typically blow from the west or northwest and are particularly prevalent in the states of Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab, and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The temperature of Loo winds can often exceed 45°C, significantly raising the ambient temperature and creating harsh living conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mango Winds**

 
 
• Mango winds are pre-monsoon showers in the coastal regions of Kerala and Karnataka in India.
 
• These winds are named so because they help in the ripening of mangoes in these regions.
 
 
 
• **Kaal Baishakhi**
 
 
• Kaal Baishakhi refers to the violent thunderstorms that occur in the eastern parts of India, particularly in West Bengal and Assam, during the pre-monsoon months of April and May.
 
• These storms are characterized by strong winds, heavy rains, and lightning, often causing significant damage to property and crops.
 
 
 
• **Trade Winds**
 
 
• Trade winds are steady winds that blow from east to west just north and south of the equator.
 
• They are part of the Earth's atmospheric circulation system and play a crucial role in maritime navigation and weather patterns across tropical regions.
